_about: PREVIEW DATA — UNVERIFIED. Structured stubs written from general knowledge so the app prototype has something to match against. Nothing here is a sourced claim. Every entry must be verified (or dropped) in Phase 2/3; researched case cards in /cases override these by id.

cases.name: Bilbao
cases.summary: Post-industrial port city paired a franchise Guggenheim museum with a broader regeneration plan (metro, riverfront, airport).
cases.lesson: The museum was the visible piece of a larger public program; copies that bought only the building mostly failed.

cases.name: Marfa, Texas
cases.summary: Artist Donald Judd bought former army buildings and ranch land; the Chinati Foundation followed. Decades later the town became a niche art destination.
cases.lesson: A single in-migrant founder can define a town for decades; housing and long-time residents feel it later.

cases.name: Santa Fe (Meow Wolf origin)
cases.summary: A local artist collective opened a permanent immersive venue in a former bowling alley, then expanded the brand to other cities.
cases.lesson: A concept born from a local art scene can scale; whether the origin town keeps capturing value after expansion is the open question.

cases.name: Anaheim
cases.summary: Orange groves became the first Disneyland; the city grew around the park and later fought over subsidies and wages.
cases.lesson: A host place gets traffic and tax base but bargains from weakness with the IP owner.

cases.name: Orlando / Reedy Creek
cases.summary: Disney assembled land quietly and obtained a self-governing special district before Walt Disney World opened in 1971.
cases.lesson: Governance concessions made to land an anchor can outlast the politics that granted them.

cases.name: Marne-la-Vallée (Disneyland Paris)
cases.summary: A state-backed new-town project landed Euro Disney with rail links; the resort struggled financially for years after opening.
cases.lesson: Public infrastructure promises are certain; the private anchor's returns are not.

cases.name: Matamata (Hobbiton)
cases.summary: A family sheep farm chosen as a film set rebuilt it permanently and runs tours; the town rebranded around it.
cases.lesson: Outside IP, but local land ownership of the set let a family capture much of the value.

cases.name: Dubrovnik
cases.summary: Walled old town with heritage status became a cruise and screen-tourism magnet; residents left the old town as visitor numbers climbed, prompting cruise and visitor limits.
cases.lesson: Designation plus cruise plus screen fame stacked demand on one tiny area faster than governance could respond.

cases.name: Venice
cases.summary: The historic center lost residents for decades as tourism grew; the city later restricted large cruise ships and introduced a day-tripper fee (2024).
cases.lesson: A place can be economically thriving as a destination while emptying as a community.

cases.name: Maya Bay, Koh Phi Phi Leh
cases.summary: Fame from the film The Beach brought boat crowds that damaged the reef; authorities closed the bay from 2018 to 2022 and reopened it with limits.
cases.lesson: Closure and caps can work ecologically, but only after damage made the case for them.

cases.name: Hallstatt
cases.summary: A lakeside village with world heritage status went viral on social media and was replicated in China; day-trip crowds now dwarf the population.
cases.lesson: A tiny place cannot absorb global-scale attention; bus and day-visitor controls came late.

cases.name: Amsterdam
cases.summary: After years of promotion, the city shifted to de-marketing, rental limits and a 'stay away' campaign aimed at party tourists (2023).
cases.lesson: A city can switch from promoting demand to deliberately shaping it, but brand reputations change slowly.

cases.name: Ubud, Bali
cases.summary: A long-standing arts village became a global wellness destination after Eat Pray Love; water, traffic and land pressures followed.
cases.lesson: A story written by outsiders can amplify real local culture and also commodify it.

cases.name: Medellín
cases.summary: 'Social urbanism': cable cars and library-parks in hillside neighborhoods, followed by a tourism and digital-nomad boom.
cases.lesson: Investment aimed at residents rebuilt the city's image, but later foreign demand brought new displacement pressure.

cases.name: Barcelona
cases.summary: The 1992 Olympics opened the waterfront and launched a tourism boom; decades later the city plans to phase out tourist apartment licenses.
cases.lesson: One of the few Olympics treated as a success, and later a model for overtourism backlash.

cases.name: Kyoto
cases.summary: Rapid inbound tourism growth strained buses and historic districts; the city restricted access to some private alleys in Gion (2024).
cases.lesson: Even a place that authors its own heritage story needs crowd management once demand is global.

cases.name: Lisbon
cases.summary: After the debt crisis, tourism, short-term rentals and foreign-resident incentives drove a boom; housing affordability became a national issue.
cases.lesson: Recovery strategies built on outside demand transferred pressure onto the housing stock.

cases.name: Bhutan
cases.summary: 'High value, low volume' tourism with a daily fee; the fee was raised in 2022 and then cut after arrivals stayed low.
cases.lesson: Pricing access protects a place, but it can overshoot what demand will bear.

cases.name: Iceland
cases.summary: After the 2008 banking collapse and the 2010 eruption, a national campaign and airline stopovers drove a tourism surge.
cases.lesson: Tourism can rescue a crisis economy fast and then become the next concentration risk.

cases.name: Palau
cases.summary: Visitors sign the 'Palau Pledge' in their passport on arrival; the country has pushed toward lower-volume, higher-value tourism.
cases.lesson: Policy design is novel; long-run outcome data is thin.

cases.name: Las Vegas
cases.summary: Nevada legalized gambling in 1931; a desert railroad town grew into a destination dominated by large corporate resorts.
cases.lesson: A first-mover legal advantage built a durable identity even after other places legalized gambling.

cases.name: Atlantic City
cases.summary: A declining resort legalized casinos to revive itself; competition from neighboring states later closed several casinos (2014) and strained city finances.
cases.lesson: A regulatory monopoly is an advantage with an expiry date.

cases.name: Detroit
cases.summary: The original Motor City lost much of its industry and population and went through municipal bankruptcy (2013).
cases.lesson: An identity built on one industry can outlive that industry's economics by decades.

cases.name: Napa Valley
cases.summary: Napa wines beat French wines at the 1976 'Judgment of Paris' tasting; the valley became a wine-tourism model, later with heavy outside ownership.
cases.lesson: Agricultural land protection kept the landscape; it did not keep wineries locally owned.

cases.name: Nashville
cases.summary: A radio show (the Grand Ole Opry, 1925) seeded a music industry that became the city's identity; it is now a bachelorette and convention magnet.
cases.lesson: An industry identity can be turned into a tourism identity; the musicians who built it are often priced out.

cases.name: Hudson, New York
cases.summary: A declining river town's intact Main Street drew antique dealers, then artists and New York City weekenders.
cases.lesson: Cheap historic stock within reach of a big metro is a strong, and gentrifying, combination.

cases.name: Taos, New Mexico
cases.summary: An early-20th-century art colony formed around Taos Pueblo and the landscape; skiing and second homes came later.
cases.lesson: Outside artists' depictions of Indigenous neighbors built the brand; authorship remains contested.

cases.name: Asheville
cases.summary: Mountain town with the Biltmore estate built a craft-beer, arts and outdoor identity; tourism exposure showed after Hurricane Helene (2024).
cases.lesson: A diversified local scene still concentrates risk if everything depends on visitors.

cases.name: Byron Bay
cases.summary: After the abattoir and whaling closed, surfers and counterculture migrants reshaped the town; it later became a celebrity and influencer brand with severe housing stress.
cases.lesson: The people who created the vibe were among the first priced out.

cases.name: Ojai, California
cases.summary: Citrus valley with early design controls and a spiritual-retreat reputation; it stayed small and became an expensive retreat for nearby Los Angeles.
cases.lesson: Limiting growth preserved character and made it exclusive.

cases.name: North Adams (MASS MoCA)
cases.summary: A huge vacant factory complex became a contemporary art museum; the town's broader economic indicators improved slowly.
cases.lesson: An anchor can succeed as an institution while the town around it changes only gradually.

cases.name: Bentonville, Arkansas
cases.summary: Walmart heirs funded Crystal Bridges museum (2011) and mountain-bike trails to make the HQ town attractive to talent.
cases.lesson: Patron money can build amenities fast; the place depends on one family and one company.

cases.name: Lowell, Massachusetts
cases.summary: A former mill city became an urban national historical park telling its own industrial story.
cases.lesson: Interpreting real industrial history is ownable; on its own it was not enough to replace the lost jobs.

cases.name: Athens 2004 Olympics
cases.summary: Transport upgrades endured, but many venues sat unused after the Games and costs added to public debt.
cases.lesson: Mega-event venues without a planned afterlife become liabilities.

cases.name: Sochi 2014 Olympics
cases.summary: Widely reported as among the most expensive Olympics; environmental damage and underused facilities followed.
cases.lesson: Top-down mega-projects can transform a place physically without creating durable demand.

cases.name: Rio de Janeiro 2016 Olympics
cases.summary: Evictions before the Games and abandoned venues after; the port-area regeneration had mixed results.
cases.lesson: Event deadlines tend to override resident protections.

cases.name: Montreal 1976 Olympics
cases.summary: The Olympic stadium debt took about three decades to pay off.
cases.lesson: The classic case for why later cities negotiated harder or declined to bid.

cases.name: Ciudad Real Central Airport
cases.summary: A privately built international airport opened in 2008 and closed within a few years for lack of traffic.
cases.lesson: Access infrastructure amplifies existing demand; it does not create it.

cases.name: Millennium Dome / The O2 (Greenwich)
cases.summary: A year-long exhibition widely judged a failure; the building later reopened as a successful arena (2007).
cases.lesson: A failed program can sit in a successful building; reuse can rescue a bad first use.

cases.name: Glasgow (European City of Culture 1990)
cases.summary: The designation and campaign repositioned an industrial city as a cultural destination; critics argued that working-class history was sidelined.
cases.lesson: A designation year can reset an image; who gets written into the new story matters.

cases.name: Pigeon Forge (Dollywood)
cases.summary: A native-born star lent her name to an existing park near her home region, next to a major national park.
cases.lesson: Branded IP doesn't have to come from outside; local-born IP changes the value-capture math.

cases.name: Italian €1-house towns (e.g. Mussomeli, Sambuca)
cases.summary: Depopulating towns sold derelict houses for a token price with renovation obligations; the schemes got global press coverage.
cases.lesson: Viral attention is easy to win; turning buyers into year-round residents is the hard part.

cases.name: Tulsa Remote
cases.summary: A local foundation pays remote workers to move to Tulsa for at least a year.
cases.lesson: Attracting residents instead of visitors is cheap to test; it is too early to judge compounding.

cases.name: Park City (Sundance)
cases.summary: A former silver-mining town became a ski resort and film-festival town; the festival announced a move to Boulder from 2027.
cases.lesson: An identity built on an event the town doesn't own can leave.

cases.name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta
cases.summary: Title was handed back to the Anangu traditional owners in 1985 under joint management; the climb was closed in 2019.
cases.lesson: Owner control lets a place say no to the most-demanded activity.

cases.name: Galápagos Islands
cases.summary: A national park with entry fees and controlled itineraries; growth of land-based tourism drew migrants and added pressure.
cases.lesson: Caps on visitor activities don't cap resident population growth driven by tourism jobs.

cases.name: Albuquerque (Breaking Bad)
cases.summary: State film incentives brought productions; a hit series created location tourism; Netflix bought a local studio (2018).
cases.lesson: A path from location to production base, though the studio is outside-owned.

cases.name: Shenzhen
cases.summary: A special economic zone hosted outside manufacturers, then grew homegrown tech and hardware firms.
cases.lesson: The clearest example of host to originator: supplier networks and skills learned from guests became local firms.

cases.name: Silicon Valley
cases.summary: Orchards became the semiconductor and software capital, built on a university, defense spending and spinoff culture.
cases.lesson: Compounding spinoffs is the strongest originator signal, and housing is its price.

cases.name: Santiago de Compostela
cases.summary: The medieval pilgrimage route was revived through heritage listing and Holy Year campaigns, spreading spending along the whole Camino.
cases.lesson: A route spreads benefits across many small towns better than a single destination can.

cases.name: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone
cases.summary: Official tours opened, then surged after an HBO series (2019); the 2022 war halted tourism.
cases.lesson: Dark tourism follows media and is exposed to geopolitics.

cases.name: Fujikawaguchiko
cases.summary: A convenience store with a viral Mt Fuji view drew such crowds that the town put up a screen to block the shot (2024).
cases.lesson: Viral demand concentrates on one spot the place never chose.

cases.name: Isle of Eigg
cases.summary: Residents bought the island from private landlords in 1997 and run land, housing and energy through a community trust.
cases.lesson: Changing who owns the land changes who captures any later growth.

cases.name: Macau
cases.summary: Opening casino licenses to foreign operators (2002) made gambling revenue exceed Las Vegas; the economy collapsed during pandemic travel limits.
cases.lesson: Extreme concentration pays well until access is cut.

cases.name: Margate
cases.summary: A faded seaside resort opened Turner Contemporary (2011) and drew London creatives; deprivation persists alongside the new scene.
cases.lesson: Culture-led renewal can coexist with persistent local deprivation.
